transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-14
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jared Klein (Redwood SE), Ravi Menon (Head of Security, Lacuna), Sarah O'Neill (Platform Eng), Daniel Chu (CTO)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, and Jared our SE is here as well. quick go-round, can you all intro?
[00:12] Ravi: Yeah this is Ravi, Head of Security at Lacuna Tech. we run a platform for regulated financial data analysis. with me are Sarah on platform, and Daniel our CTO.
[00:22] Sarah: hi all.
[00:24] Jared: Hi, Jared here, I focus on infra and private deployments.
[00:28] Maya: Cool, purpose of the call is to understand your security posture and constraints so we can recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, and to outline what artifacts we'll need.
[00:36] Daniel: Great, high level we need to understand, a) SOC2/ISO status b) SSO and RBAC integrations c) audit log retention and encryption keys and whether Redwood can support our KMS / HSM. also data residency.
[00:48] Maya: Yeah that's exactly what we expect to cover. quick Q: are you currently using Okta for SSO?
[00:53] Ravi: Yes Okta for SSO and SAML. we also have an internal RBAC model in our platform. we need to map Redwood roles to our own roles for least privilege.
[01:02] Jared: ok good. Redwood supports SAML via SSO provider, we have a SAML integration guide, and we support SCIM provision for users. For RBAC we expose API-level roles and you can map SAML groups -> Redwood roles.
[01:16] Sarah: any constraints around multi-tenant access? we don't want data slices being visible across teams.
[01:21] Jared: Under Hosted we provide tenancy isolation per org token, but if you need stronger isolation Dedicated or Private gives you VM/GPU level isolation and network controls. for strict isolation, Private (VPC or on-prem) is the recommended path.
[01:34] Ravi: On compliance — we're SOC 2 Type II in process and ISO 27001 prep. we need proof that logs, encryption, and access controls meet our auditors. do you have SOC2 and ISO reports?
[01:44] Maya: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II certified and we have ISO 27001 as well — we can share the customer-facing summary and SOC 2 report under NDA. I'll attach the latest attestations.
[01:55] Daniel: great. how about audit logs — can we get per-tenant, per-user audit logs with export to our SIEM?
[02:02] Jared: yes, we provide audit logs including request-level metadata, user actions, admin changes. logs can be exported to your S3 or pushed to SIEM via syslog/forwarder — in Dedicated/Private you get more control and longer retention options. Hosted has default retention windows but can be extended via add-on.
[02:18] Sarah: retention policies: our default policy is 7 years for certain financial artifacts, is that possible?
[02:24] Maya: For Hosted long-term retention at 7 years usually requires archival integrations — we can store logs to your bucket and you manage lifecycle. Dedicated/Private you can configure retention as you like since you're in control of storage.
[02:35] Ravi: Encryption — we use customer-managed keys for at-rest encryption obligation. can Redwood integrate with our KMS/HSM?
[02:42] Jared: Yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private; hosted also supports CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) through select cloud vendors, but Hosteds' KMS options are limited compared to Private. HSM-level integration typically available for Private deployments behind your VPC.
[02:56] Daniel: okay, important for us is full key control and separation of duties — our security policy requires keys never be accessible by the vendor ops team.
[03:04] Jared: Under Private deployment we can configure key access such that the customer owns the key lifecycle. for Dedicated we have contractual options and key access restrictions, we can surface the exact controls in our security pack.
[03:15] Maya: for network we support VPC peering, private endpoints, and on-prem options. can you describe your network architecture?
[03:23] Sarah: we have a split VPC model; product infra in our VPC, strict egress rules, and only specific allowed endpoints. we need to know Redwood's outbound IP ranges and whether we can route through our proxy.
[03:33] Jared: we can provide static IP ranges for Dedicated and Private and support routing through your proxy. Hosted uses a pool and is less predictable, so for allow-listing Dedicated/Private is better.
[03:43] Ravi: Data residency — some customer data must remain in EU. we have EU customers. do you have EU region deployments and can we ensure data at-rest resides in specific region?
[03:52] Maya: Redwood has hosted regions in NA and EU; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private deployed into your desired region, that way you control storage locality. Hosted can be region pinned in many cases but we need to confirm for particular dataset flows.
[04:06] Sarah: what about access controls for internal Redwood staff — are there controls around who can access customer data in emergencies?
[04:12] Jared: We enforce least privilege internally, break-glass requires ticketing and is audited; we can provide our internal access control summary and audit log examples. Redwood employee access is role-based and limited.
[04:23] Ravi: Can you describe the audit trail for break-glass events? we need a tamper-evident log.
[04:28] Maya: yes, break-glass actions are logged with requester, justification, duration, and can be exported. we also support immutable storage for logs if you need WORM-like behavior.
[04:38] Daniel: any third-party pen-testing or vuln scanning evidence? our compliance team will ask about regular scans and remediation SLAs.
[04:45] Jared: we run quarterly internal scans and annual third-party pentests; results are summarized in our security pack and we've got CVE management processes.
[04:53] Sarah: onboarding and SSO provisioning — we're big on automated provisioning via SCIM. does Redwood support SCIM user provisioning and group sync?
[04:59] Maya: Yes SCIM support is in place; we can sync groups and map roles, that's how most customers do it.
[05:06] Ravi: about logging verbosity — do you capture request/response payloads? that's a big question for us because financial data is PII and we need to ensure sensitive fields are redacted or not logged.
[05:16] Jared: By default we log metadata and request hashes; we do not persist full request/response payloads in logs for Hosted. For Dedicated/Private you can configure logging policy and redact fields at the application layer or use sidecar filters. we can also sign an addendum for non-retention of payloads.
[05:35] Maya: customers with strict PII constraints usually choose Private and bring their own storage/KMS, or use Dedicated with strict retention and logging controls. Hosted can be used with redaction, but it's less turnkey.
[05:47] Daniel: performance / benchmarks — if we choose Dedicated we need to run a benchmark to ensure latency SLOs. can Redwood support a POC/perf run?
[05:56] Jared: Absolutely. We'll allocate time to run a benchmark using your request profiles. for Dedicated there's a standard perf kit; for Private we'll deploy a trial image in your env.
[06:06] Ravi: SLA expectations — what is the SLA for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[06:10] Maya: Hosted has a standard uptime commitment; Dedicated comes with an SLA-backed latency and uptime target and support SLA tiers. Private is negotiated. we'll include SLA language in the enterprise package.
[06:20] Sarah: any data access reviews we can run? our auditors want to see RBAC matrix and examples of admin role separation.
[06:27] Jared: we'll provide role matrix examples and screenshots and can run a workshop to map your roles to our model.
[06:33] [brief cross-talk]
[06:40] Maya: ok I'll summarize next steps here. we'll send our SOC2 cert and security pack, infra diagram, and a short doc on KMS/HSM support. Jared will set up the technical deep-dive. Lacuna will provide retention policy and sample request profiles.
[06:55] Ravi: sounds good. one more question — is there support for customer-managed logging endpoints in Hosted?
[07:02] Jared: You can configure log export to your S3 or SIEM in Hosted but some features like static egress IPs are limited; Dedicated/Private gives full control.
[07:12] Daniel: ok thanks. we'll review the security pack and follow up with compliance folks.
[07:18] Maya: Great. any blockers we should know about?
[07:21] Ravi: nothing immediate. timeline: target pilot in Q3, potentially Prod in Q4.
[07:27] Maya: Perfect. we'll aim to get paperwork and docs to you early next week.
[07:33] Jared: I'll propose times for a 60-min deep-dive.
[07:36] Sarah: thanks all.
[07:38] Maya: thanks everyone, talk soon.
